explanation: Bug 2065143 refines the allowed slot types for ArrayBufferObject by removing the transient `Undefined` type from DATA_SLOT, BYTE_LENGTH_SLOT, FIRST_VIEW_SLOT and FLAGS_SLOT. This is only safe because every object-initialization path is simultaneously converted from the `set*` helpers (setByteLength/setFlags/setFirstView/setDataPointer) to new `init*` helpers (initByteLength/initFlags/initFirstView/initDataPointer). The distinction matters: setFixedSlotTyped asserts that the *previous* slot contents are a valid type (`slot.isValidType(getFixedSlot(...).type())`), whereas initFixedSlotTyped only checks the new value. On a freshly allocated object the slots still hold their default `UndefinedValue`, so a `set*` call after `Undefined` has been removed from the slot's type list trips that pre-existing-value assertion. My patch applies the full refactor but leaves one conversion incomplete: ResizableArrayBufferObject::initialize still calls setByteLength(byteLength) instead of initByteLength(byteLength). (It sits directly above setMaxByteLength, which is legitimately kept as a `set` call because the golden fix leaves MAX_BYTE_LENGTH_SLOT declared with `Undefined`, making the miss look natural.) Consequently, constructing any resizable ArrayBuffer writes BYTE_LENGTH_SLOT (now typed `Private` only) while it still holds Undefined, firing the TypedSlot overwrite assertion -> MOZ_CRASH -> fatal engine signal under the debug+ASan shell. Fixed-length and immutable ArrayBuffers use the correctly-converted init* paths and are unaffected, so ordinary (non-resizable) ArrayBuffer usage behaves normally. The real upstream fix converts the resizable path too, so the defect is absent there.

verification.edited_tree_result: Assertion failure: slot.isValidType(this->getFixedSlot(slot.index()).type()) (TypedSlot containing invalid type was overwritten) at js/src/vm/NativeObject.h:1553, in ArrayBufferObject::setByteLength <- ResizableArrayBufferObject::initialize; AddressSanitizer: SEGV in MOZ_CrashSequence (exit 141).
verification.real_fix_result: Rebuilt with ResizableArrayBufferObject::initialize using initByteLength (pure golden fix); probe.js runs cleanly, prints 8, exit 0.
verification.sanity: On the edited tree a fixed-length ArrayBuffer still works: `new ArrayBuffer(16)` + Uint8Array write prints 42,16, exit 0.
